content.text:
I made one more fix, but it's an educated guess because I still haven't seen the body of the request at `errors_auth.hurl:204`. `./mvnw -q verify` passes, including a new regression test, but I haven't rerun the Hurl suite.

**How I looked for it:** I ran the current code on port 8091 and sent about 20 invalid bodies to `PUT /api/user`. These returned 200:

| Body | Result |
|---|---|
| `{"user":{"bio":123}}`, `{"user":{"username":true}}` | 200: the number or boolean was quietly saved as text |
| `{"user":{"username":"OTHER…"}}` (an existing name in different upper/lower case) | 200 |
| `{"user":{"email":"foo@bar"}}` | 200 |
| `{"user":{"image":"not-a-url"}}`, `{"user":{"password":"a"}}`, `{"user":{"username":"has space"}}`, `bio` with 5000 characters | 200 |

**What I fixed:** wrong JSON types. The spec says these fields are `string`, but the API accepted numbers and booleans and saved them as text. Of all the rows above, this is the only one the contract clearly forbids.

- **New `shared/config/JacksonConfig.java`:** numbers and booleans sent where text is expected are now rejected. This applies to every endpoint, including registration and login.
